description: Talent pipeline index: research output quality (35%, OpenAlex), domestic PhD pipeline (25%, NSF/MoE), and elite researcher concentration + migration (40%, MacroPolo). See talent_manual.json for pipeline and migration data sources.

pipeline.confidence: High — government survey covering all US PhD-granting institutions

elite_migration.confidence: Medium-High — systematic methodology on public conference proceedings; lag of 1-2 years from latest venue; elite venue selection may not capture applied AI research
elite_migration.migration_note: China's domestic retention of China-origin top researchers has increased from ~25% (2019 cohort) to ~34% (2022 cohort). The US share has declined slightly but remains dominant.

pipeline.source: China Ministry of Education (MoE) Statistics 2022 / 教育部统计数据
pipeline.confidence: Medium — official statistics, but classification of 'AI-related' is broader than Western definitions; peer-reviewed verification limited
pipeline.coverage_note: China MoE 2022 reports ~52,000 CS/IT-category doctoral graduates. Estimated 30% are AI/ML-adjacent. China's broad CS classification includes applied software engineering that would not typically be classified as AI research in Western databases. Adjusted estimate is conservative. Note: a significant share of top Chinese AI researchers do their PhD in the US or Europe.

elite_migration.confidence: Medium-High — systematic methodology on public conference proceedings; lag of 1-2 years from latest venue; elite venue selection may not capture applied AI research
elite_migration.migration_note: China's domestic retention of China-origin top researchers has increased from ~25% (2019 cohort) to ~34% (2022 cohort). The US share has declined slightly but remains dominant.

openalex.methodology_note: Papers counted once per country where ≥1 author has an identified institution. Multinational papers counted in both countries — sums exceed total paper count. High-impact and top-cited queries add a cited_by_count filter which may not work on all OpenAlex instances (falls back to seeded estimates if the filter returns zero results). OpenAlex does not de-duplicate authors across papers; a prolific researcher counts once per paper, not once per researcher.

coverage_warning: Three measurement gaps affect all talent assessments: (1) Affiliation vs. origin — a China-born researcher working at MIT is counted under the US, inflating the US share in publication-based metrics; (2) Quality vs. quantity — China produces 3-5x the PhD volume but the US captures a disproportionate share of elite researchers at frontier labs; (3) Migration direction — the US has historically attracted China-born AI talent, but return migration to China has accelerated since ~2019.

LONGITUDINAL DEVICE MIGRATION AND MEANING CONTINUITY AT THE LIMIT Device Replacement × Model Bridging × Control Semantics STARLI RESEARCH WORKS | INSTITUTE XXIV | FLAGSHIP 24 Feng Cheng-en 33 × Starli Research Works This research monograph investigates a deceptively difficult question in long-term brain–computer interfaces: when sensors, acquisition electronics, firmware, electrode geometry, or decoding models change, what would justify the claim that a user's task-grounded control meaning has been preserved? Numerical signal alignment alone cannot establish continuity of intention. Two systems may encode different signals while supporting the same functional command, or produce nearly identical latent representations while mapping to incompatible actions. The volume formulates meaning continuity as a conditional, falsifiable engineering and scientific hypothesis. It connects device-specific observation models, neural recording instability, task and action ontologies, paired old/new sensing periods, latent manifold bridging, longitudinal recalibration, calibrated abstention, functional validation, and an accessible right to reject the proposed migration. Its central commitment is that no amount of predictive accuracy can compensate for invalid authorization, an unverified physical reference, or loss of independent control. The research atlas comprises thirty connected mathematical derivations, eighty-two research chapters, and 410 independently paginated chapter sections that examine observables, inverse explanations, discriminating experiments, uncertainty and noncompensable safeguards, and independent requalification. Two hundred detailed Research Gates propose future falsification and handoff programs, while thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos preserve revisable candidate approaches rather than immutable conclusions. A claim-scoped DOI evidence ledger connects the study to published work on neural recording drift, decoder adaptation, manifold alignment, longitudinal neural interfaces, speech BCIs, user preferences, and neurotechnology ethics. The book is designed for both human researchers and future AI research systems. Its formulas, chapter cross-links, DOI anchors, competing models, negative-result requirements, and successor-focused research cards provide structured entry points for independent reconstruction and informed disagreement. The visual presentation combines ivory pages, navy and teal typography, and large gold mathematical plates, while mathematical expressions are also recorded in searchable source notation and a separate Excel reference index. This is a prospective, nonclinical research architecture. It does not report new patient experiments, demonstrate safe autonomous human neurovascular microrobots, establish a universal device-migration system, or claim continuity of private thoughts, consciousness, or personal identity. Scientific benefit remains conditional on explicit task definitions, qualified device evidence, legitimate permissions, external validation, and the successor's freedom to reject a failed bridge. Research question: What should remain invariant when an interface changes, and who has the authority to say that its meaning has changed?
